entries.title: Judges 6:1
segments:
Midian; the Midianites lived east of the south part of Palestine. 
 
Unless the grace of God prevent, men naturally incline to sin, showing that in them, without the grace of God, there is no spiritually good thing.

entries.title: Judges 6:3
segments: Amalekites, and the children of the east; neighboring tribes to the Midianites.  By the "children of the east" Arabian tribes seem to be especially intended.

entries.title: Judges 6:4
segments:
Gaza; a city of the Philistines in the south-west part of Palestine, on the Mediterranean. 
 
Sin tends to misery, and all the calamities which men suffer are tokens of God's displeasure against it.

entries.title: Judges 6:5
segments: To destroy it; take away the means of sustenance.

entries.title: Judges 6:7
segments: The only hope of deliverance from sin and its consequences is in the Lord; and when men feel this, and cry unto him, he for Christ's sake often appears for their help.

entries.title: Judges 6:10
segments:
Fear not the gods; not worship or serve them. 
 
When God is about to grant deliverance to his people, he first convinces them that sin is the cause of their troubles and leads them to forsake it.

entries.title: Judges 6:11
segments: Angel of the Lord; this is supposed to have been the Angel of the covenant, who brought Israel out of Egypt, Jehovah-Jesus.

Ophrah; a city in the tribe of Benjamin. 
 
  By the wine-press; a retired and covered place, where the Midianites would not be likely to find it.

entries.title: Judges 6:12
segments: Providence developes human character.  Many who have been buried for a time in obscurity, have afterwards, by peculiar circumstances, been raised to elevated positions of influence, usefulness, and honor.

entries.title: Judges 6:14
segments: Looked; looked efficaciously.
A look from the Lord can nerve the self-diffident for the most perilous services; and fit them, notwithstanding all difficulties, to go on in his name and strength from conquering to conquer.

entries.title: Judges 6:16
segments: As one man; as easily and effectually as if there were but one man.

entries.title: Judges 6:17
segments: Show me a sign; evidence that it is Jehovah who speaks to me, and that his word will be accomplished.

entries.title: Judges 6:18
segments: God is ready to give evidence of his truth to all sincere inquirers who wish to understand his will for the purpose of doing it.

entries.title: Judges 6:24
segments:
Shalom; meaning peace. 
 
All the manifestations of God to his believing, obedient people will lead them anew to adore and bless him.

entries.title: Judges 6:25
segments: Strong faith in God's word will be tried, and thus fit the believer, by patient continuance in well-doing, to be made victorious and perfect.

entries.title: Judges 6:28
segments: The grove; here, as often elsewhere, the Hebrew word rendered "grove" seems to mean a wooden image of Astarte, fixed by a post in the ground.

entries.title: Judges 6:31
segments:
Joash said; though he seems to have been a worshipper of Baal, his views may have been changed by what Gideon had told him. 
 
  Whilst it is yet morning; his folly in pleading for Baal, who, if really a God, ought to take care of himself.  Joash said this to dissuade the people from their purpose. 
 
Idolatry so debases men, and renders them so foolish, that they will worship, and sometimes try to help gods that have no power to help themselves.

entries.title: Judges 6:32
segments: Jerubbaal; that is, let Baal plead.

entries.title: Judges 6:34
segments:
Abi-ezer; the family of his father, and his relatives. 
 
If men are to be fitted for good, great, and noble deeds, it must be through the influences of the Spirit of God.  Wisdom, strength, courage, energy, and perseverance are his gifts, and to him they should, by all who possess them, be heartily devoted.

entries.title: Judges 6:37
segments: Evidence of the presence and favor of God, and a conviction of being engaged in his work, support the soul under trials, arm it for conflicts, and prepare it, notwithstanding all difficulties and dangers, in his name to triumph.
